briefings.takeaway: Dry, sunny, and hot again. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) says a mass of dry air over Central America keeps rain odds low all week, with few clouds on the North Pacific today and Nicoya near 35°C. Surf stays offshore every morning through at least Saturday. The new long-period swell is in today, 4–6 ft at 17 seconds, and holds in the 16-second range through Thursday, with the trades getting stronger Thursday night into Friday. October ends dry. The early-November wet spell came back a bit stronger overnight, now centered around Nov 4–6. No tropical threat, and the prolonged-rain watch stays low.

Another dry, sunny, breezy day. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has few clouds and gusty morning trade winds on the North Pacific today, with no rain in the forecast here, and Nicoya near 34°C. Surf stays offshore every day through at least Friday. Today has the most size, 5–7 ft at 13 seconds, and a new long-period swell (16–17 seconds) now shows up Tuesday, a day sooner than yesterday's call, and runs through Thursday. The rest of October looks dry. The models still show a few showery days around Nov 3–7, a little weaker and more spread out than yesterday. No tropical threat, and the prolonged-rain watch stays low.

A dry, sunny, gusty Sunday. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has few clouds and strong morning trade-wind gusts on the North Pacific today, with no rain in the forecast here; the showers stay on the Central and South Pacific. Nicoya should reach about 34°C. For surf, it's offshore every day through at least Thursday, with 4–6 feet at 13–14 seconds today and Monday and a new long-period pulse (15–16 seconds) from Tuesday night into Thursday. The rest of October looks mostly dry. The models still show a wetter stretch around Nov 2–6, a bit stronger today and centered near Nov 4, while IMN still expects the dry season to settle in. No tropical threat to Costa Rica, and the prolonged-rain watch stays low.

Hot and sunny this morning, with a better chance than yesterday of a passing afternoon shower or thunderstorm on the Nicoya Peninsula. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has few clouds and gusty trade winds this morning, then scattered showers on the peninsula this afternoon. Nicoya should hit about 35°C. For surf, it's offshore every day through at least Wednesday, with a 4–6 foot, 14-second swell today and Sunday, a shorter-period day Monday, then a new long-period pulse Tuesday night into Wednesday. Next week looks mostly dry. The models still show a wetter spell around Nov 2–6, while IMN still expects the dry season to settle in during early November. No tropical threat to Costa Rica, and the prolonged-rain watch stays low.

Another hot, mostly sunny day. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has few clouds on the North Pacific this morning, light winds early, and a few clouds building this afternoon with only an isolated shower in the hills. Nicoya should hit about 35°C. For surf, it's offshore again today and every day through at least Tuesday, with a south-southwest swell at 5–7 feet and 15 seconds today, easing to 3–5 feet by Sunday, then a new longer-period pulse showing up Tuesday night. The rest of October looks mostly dry. The models are still pointing to a wetter spell around Nov 2–5, now a little earlier and a little stronger, while IMN still calls for the dry season to arrive in early November. No tropical threat to Costa Rica, and the prolonged-rain watch stays low.

Another sunny, breezy, hot day. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has few clouds this morning on the North Pacific, a chance of scattered showers on the peninsula this afternoon, and Nicoya near 34°C. The trade winds pick up a notch today as the season's first cold push brushes the region, with gusts of 30–45 km/h possible in Guanacaste. For surf, it's offshore today and every day through at least Monday, with a 17-second south-southwest swell at 5–7 feet today, easing over the weekend. The rest of October looks mostly dry. The one new wrinkle is that the models now bring a wetter spell close to Nosara around Nov 3–5, which goes against IMN's dry outlook. No tropical threat to Costa Rica, and the prolonged-rain watch stays low.

The turn to trade winds is here. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has a mostly sunny day on the North Pacific, with only a low chance of an isolated afternoon shower on the Nicoya Peninsula and Nicoya near 34°C. Northeast breezes hold over Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica for the next two weeks, and IMN now expects the dry season to settle in on the North Pacific during the week of Oct 25–Nov 1. For surf, it's offshore today and every day through Sunday, with a long-period south-southwest swell (about 18 seconds today). This is the best wind-and-swell combo in a while. No tropical threat to Costa Rica, and the prolonged-rain watch stays low.

One more humid, showery day, then the pattern turns. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has Nicoya near 34°C today with isolated afternoon storms and coastal showers around the peninsula tonight. From Wednesday the Caribbean trades push back in, and the models now spread that breeze over the Nicoya Peninsula from Thursday into early next week, with rain shifting to the Caribbean side. For surf, today's wind is southeast to south (side-on to onshore), so it's a so-so day. Offshore northeast winds return Wednesday, with a firmer push Thursday. No tropical threat to Costa Rica, and the prolonged-rain watch drops a notch.

A warm, humid Monday with scattered afternoon storms possible along the North Pacific coast. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has Nicoya near 34–35°C and keeps the band of tropical showers close to the country. Ensemble averages still look showery through about Wednesday, then lighter. For surf, east (offshore) winds today at about 10–15 knots; Tuesday afternoon may flip side-on or onshore, then a firmer northeast-to-east Papagayo pulse returns Wednesday night into Thursday. Tropical Storm Trudy and a likely new storm midweek both stay well off Mexico and move away from us. Multi-day soaking rain remains watch only.

A warm, humid Sunday with a chance of a passing shower this morning near the coast and isolated afternoon storms. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) expects the heaviest afternoon rain in the mountains today, with only scattered rain along the coast. Nicoya should reach about 34°C. Showers stay likely Monday through about Wednesday (Oct 19–21) as a tropical wave passes and the band of tropical showers sits near the coast. The models still agree on drier, breezier trade-wind weather from about Oct 23–25. For surf, this morning has an east (offshore) wind and a long-period southwest swell. The trades soften to a side-on southeast breeze Monday and Tuesday, then return as offshore east to northeast winds from Tuesday night into Thursday. Hurricane Trudy and a likely new storm midweek both stay far off Mexico. Multi-day soaking rain is still only a watch, and a notch lower than yesterday.

A hot, steamy Saturday with afternoon storms likely. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) expects a partly cloudy morning, then a mostly cloudy afternoon with downpours and thunderstorms, and it names the Nicoya Peninsula among the spots with the heaviest rain. Nicoya should reach about 34°C. Rain chances stay up from Sunday through about Thursday (Oct 18–22) as a tropical wave passes and the band of tropical showers sits close to the coast. The models then agree on drier, breezier trade-wind weather from about Oct 24. For surf, the Caribbean trades are blowing: northeast today, firmer Sunday, and east through Tuesday. That makes mornings Saturday to Tuesday (Oct 17–20) offshore at Nosara, with the swell peaking today and Sunday. Hurricane Trudy and a likely new storm next week both stay far off Mexico. Multi-day soaking rain is still only a watch, a notch higher than yesterday for Oct 20–22.

A quieter, hot Friday after yesterday's soak. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has the North Pacific mostly sunny this morning, with only scattered afternoon showers or storms possible, and Nicoya near 34°C. The shower band sits offshore over the Pacific, so local heating drives today's weather. For surf, a light northeast wind this morning fades to light and variable later; the Caribbean trades firm up Saturday and strengthen Sunday through Tuesday, so Saturday to about Tuesday (Oct 17–20) is the offshore stretch to plan around, with swell building into the weekend. Hurricane Trudy and Tropical Storm Simon stay well off Mexico. A new low may form south of Mexico next week (about 60% chance) and drift west, away from us. Multi-day soaking rain stays watch-only and looks less likely than yesterday for late next week.

Wet start in spots, then a hot day with afternoon storms. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) put out an alert overnight: Nicoya got about 35 mm (1.4 inches) in six hours Wednesday evening, and more heavy coastal rain is possible this morning. After that, expect a few clouds, scattered afternoon downpours with thunder, and a high near 35°C in Nicoya. For surf, this morning has a light northeast wind that fades by afternoon. Friday is a light north wind as a long-period swell (19 seconds) fills in. The Caribbean trades are back Saturday and build Sunday night into Monday, so Saturday through about Tuesday (Oct 17–20) is still the offshore stretch to plan around, with the swell getting a bit bigger Saturday night. Hurricane Trudy and a possible new storm next week are both far to the west, off Mexico. Multi-day soaking rain is still watch-only, with the window now about Oct 20–25.

Today is hot and mostly fair this morning, with a chance of an early shower near the coast and scattered storms this afternoon that may linger into the evening. Nicoya should reach about 34°C. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) says the tropical shower band is moving back over the country, so today and Thursday are the wettest days of the week, though storms should stay hit-or-miss on our side of the North Pacific. For surf, it's light wind with onshore afternoons through Thursday, then a big upgrade: a new long-period swell (19 seconds) arrives Thursday night, and the Caribbean trades are back from Saturday, building to 10–15 knots from the east on Sunday. Saturday through about Tuesday (Oct 17–20) is the offshore stretch to plan around. Tropical Storm Trudy formed well south of Mexico and is heading away from us. Multi-day soaking rain is still watch-only, with the window now about Oct 21–25.

A hot, mostly dry morning, then a chance of scattered downpours with thunder this afternoon. Nicoya is near 34°C, a couple of degrees hotter than yesterday. Wednesday and Thursday look a bit wetter, with a chance of an early shower on the coast and stronger afternoon storms. For surf, the wind is light this week and goes onshore in the afternoons. Your best bets are dawn sessions on a solid 6–8 foot, 16-second south-southwest swell. The Caribbean trades come back Saturday night, and Sunday through about Wednesday (Oct 18–21) looks like the next offshore stretch. The storm the hurricane center is watching is about to form well south of Mexico and is heading away from us. Multi-day soaking rain is still watch-only. The window to watch is now about Oct 21–24, and it's a little more likely than yesterday because a second major model now shows it.

A typical rainy-season Monday: a few showers along the coast early, then a partly cloudy morning, then scattered downpours with thunder this afternoon and some scattered rain on the peninsula tonight (Nicoya near 32°C). For surf, this morning is the pick of the week: the Caribbean trades are still blowing, so the wind is east to southeast, offshore to cross-offshore, on a solid 5–7 foot, 17-second south-southwest swell. The trades fade tonight. Tuesday starts light, then the wind goes onshore Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday. Thursday and Friday look light from the north, which is better but not true offshore. The storm the hurricane center is watching will form well south of Mexico and head away from us. Multi-day soaking rain stays watch-only. The window to keep an eye on has moved to about Oct 20–23, and the trades look set to return around Oct 17–22.

The tropical wave has passed, and today is a normal rainy-season Sunday: a sunny, warm morning (Nicoya near 33°C), then downpours with thunder this afternoon and some scattered rain this evening. For surf, the Caribbean trades blow offshore at Nosara this morning and again Monday morning, and the swell builds to 5–7 feet with long periods tonight into Monday. Monday afternoon the wind starts swinging onshore, and Tuesday through Thursday look light and mostly onshore. A storm the hurricane center is watching will form far to the west, off southern Mexico, and won't affect us. Multi-day soaking rain stays watch-only, with Oct 16–19 the stretch to keep an eye on, and the trades look set to return around Oct 19–23.

Tropical wave day. The wave is crossing Costa Rica today, earlier than the 'Saturday night' timing in yesterday's outlook. Expect a few showers possible before noon, then stronger storms this afternoon and evening, with rain lingering on the North Pacific tonight. Costa Rica's weather service has an alert out and flags already-soaked soils in Guanacaste. Nicoya tops out near 34°C. Sunday and Monday bring the Caribbean trade winds, which blow offshore at Nosara, so those are the clean surf mornings. From Tuesday the marine forecast swings the wind onshore from the west and northwest. The low the hurricane center is watching has shifted west toward Mexico, well away from us. Multi-day soaking rain stays watch-only, and Oct 15–19 is the stretch to keep an eye on.

A hot, sticky Friday with a dry morning and a chance of isolated afternoon storms. Nicoya could reach about 36°C. A tropical wave now arrives Saturday night, a day later than expected, so the weekend gets a bit wetter. The Caribbean trade winds, which blow offshore at Nosara, still build Sunday and peak Monday, though the marine forecast now calls them a touch lighter. A long-period south-southwest swell keeps running, with a bigger pulse around Monday. No storm threatens Costa Rica. Multi-day soaking rain stays watch-only, with Oct 16–20 the stretch to keep an eye on.

Still classic rainy season for the next few days: warm, partly cloudy mornings with a chance of an early coastal shower, then afternoon thunderstorms, with a tropical wave passing Friday. The Caribbean trade winds, which blow offshore at Nosara, still arrive Sunday, but the marine forecast now cuts them shorter, turning the wind southeast to south by Monday night. The models still keep the trades going through much of next week, so treat Sunday and Monday mornings as the surest offshore window. A long-period south-southwest swell keeps running, with a fresh pulse due early next week. No storm threatens Costa Rica. Multi-day soaking rain stays watch-only, with a small uptick in the Oct 16–19 signal.

More of the same rainy-season rhythm for now: hot, mostly sunny mornings, then afternoon storms, with a chance of early-morning showers along the coast as a tropical wave passes Friday. The bigger news is the wind. The marine forecast now shows the Caribbean trade winds arriving Sunday, turning northeast to east by Sunday night, which is offshore for Nosara. All the models agree those trades hold for most of next week, which should mean cleaner surf mornings and a drier Pacific side. A long-period south-southwest swell is already running. No storms threaten Costa Rica. Multi-day soaking rain stays watch-only, and slightly less likely than yesterday.

Classic rainy-season week: hot, sticky mornings, then afternoon storms, and Costa Rica's weather service says rain may hang on into the evening in Guanacaste today. A tropical wave arrives Friday and boosts the odds of morning rain on the coast Thursday through Sunday. For surf, winds stay light and variable today and Wednesday, then turn northwest (side-onshore at Nosara) Thursday into the weekend, so dawn is the only clean window. A long-period southwest swell builds from Wednesday. The models hint at real Caribbean trade winds (offshore for us) coming back around Oct 11–13. No storms threaten Costa Rica; the main system is forming off southern Mexico. Multi-day soaking rain is still watch-only, with one model family wetter for Oct 12–17.

Slightly quieter Sunday locally: Costa Rica’s weather service sees a partial humidity dip and more isolated afternoon showers across Pacífico Norte, with Nicoya heat still sharp (around 35°C). Surf winds stay mostly Pacific/onshore — a light morning easterly near Papagayo today is not all-day glass, then flow trends south to southwest into midweek; a brief weak easterly window may return around Wednesday mornings. Distant East Pacific storms stay well away; a new low south of southern Mexico now has a very high (~90%) chance of forming within a week and should drift west-northwest along Mexico. Prolonged multi-day rain remains watch-only, with a midweek–weekend wetter pulse possible but not a locked washout.

Sticky Pacific-moisture weekend: Costa Rica’s service flags the ITCZ still active, with possible early showers on western Nicoya and isolated afternoon rains across Pacífico Norte; Nicoya heat stays sharp (around 34°C). Surf winds remain Pacific/onshore — Papagayo light/variable Saturday after a brief morning easterly, with southwest–west elsewhere, then south to southwest into early next week; early checks only, not glassy all-day offshore. Distant East Pacific storms (Hurricane Rachel near Baja, Hurricane Nolo west of Hawaii) stay well away; a new low south of southern Mexico still has a high (~80%) chance of forming within a week and should drift west-northwest. Prolonged multi-day rain remains watch-only.

Hot, sticky Friday under an active Pacific moisture band: possible early coastal showers in northern Pacific Costa Rica, then mostly cloudy with scattered afternoon storms; rains can linger near the coast tonight. Surf winds stay Pacific/onshore — Papagayo is light/variable today (not glassy offshore), trending west to southwest this weekend and south–southwest early next week; early checks only. Distant East Pacific storms stay near Baja and Hawaii; a new low south of southern Mexico now has a high (~80%) chance of forming within a week. Prolonged multi-day rain remains watch-only.

Hot, sticky Thursday with Tropical Wave #48 nearby: morning partly cloudy, then scattered afternoon showers and storms in northern Pacific Costa Rica. Surf winds stay Pacific/onshore (west–northwest today, then west to southwest through the weekend) — expect choppier faces; early checks only, not all-day glass. Distant East Pacific storms stay near Mexico and farther west; a new low south of southern Mexico now has a high chance of forming later this week into next. Prolonged multi-day rain remains watch-only.

Hot and humid Wednesday with a clearer Pacific breeze: morning partly cloudy, then isolated afternoon downpours — plan outdoors early. Surf winds: a brief morning northeasterly at Papagayo fades to light/variable today; Thursday turns west–northwest and Friday–weekend lean Pacific/onshore (choppier). Watch Tropical Wave #48 late week for a wetter pulse. Distant East Pacific storms stay near Mexico and farther west. Prolonged multi-day rain remains watch-only.

Hot local-factor Tuesday: sunny morning, then isolated afternoon storms — showers look more scattered than the wet weekend, but a strong cell can still dump hard nearby. Surf winds: northerly/offshore today through Wednesday (best night and morning glass); Thursday softens and Friday leans Pacific/onshore. Watch Tropical Wave #48 later this week for a wetter pulse. Distant East Pacific storms stay near Mexico and farther west. Prolonged multi-day rain remains watch-only.

Quiet start to the week after Tropical Wave #47: Pacífico Norte looks mostly sunny this morning, then isolated afternoon showers on the peninsula — not a widespread storm day. Surf winds: light and mixed today, then cleaner night/morning offshore Mon night through Wednesday as Caribbean easterlies rebuild; Thursday looks softer again. Distant East Pacific storms stay near Mexico and farther west. Prolonged multi-day rain remains watch-only.

Tropical Wave #47 has moved off into the Pacific — Sunday is a quieter Pacífico Norte day with isolated afternoon showers, not yesterday’s widespread storms. Surf winds: Pacific onshore/side-on today (choppier after mid-morning); Caribbean easterlies rebuild Mon night through midweek for cleaner night/morning glass. Distant East Pacific activity stays along southern Mexico and farther west. Prolonged multi-day rain is now a watch-only, not an elevated weekend threat.

Tropical Wave #47 is over Costa Rica today — expect a partly cloudy morning, then stronger afternoon showers and storms across the northern Pacific, with some coastal rain possible into the evening. Surf winds: early-morning easterly help, then Pacific onshore later today and Sunday (choppier faces). Midweek looks cleaner as Caribbean trades rebuild. Distant East Pacific storms stay well off Mexico; prolonged multi-day rain is still a watch, not locked in.

Typical rainy-season Friday for northern Pacific Costa Rica: partly cloudy mornings, afternoon showers and storms, and a chance of coastal rain at night. Hot inland (about 35°C in Nicoya, 36.5°C in Liberia). Surf winds stay onshore from the Pacific — choppier faces, not classic easterly glass. Hurricane Polo is Category 5 well off southwestern Mexico; another system may form near Tehuantepec later and track along southern Mexico — nothing near Costa Rica. Prolonged multi-day rain watch is elevated but not locked in. A tropical wave this weekend could bump Saturday–Sunday afternoon rains a bit.

IMN Thursday keeps Pacífico Norte in rainy-season mode: morning little–partly cloudy, afternoon showers with storms over the center and south of the region, and a possible night shower near the Gulf of Nicoya (Nicoya ~32°C; Liberia ~36°C). Hurricane Polo remains a major hurricane well offshore southwestern Mexico, Hurricane Odalys stays far west in the open EPAC, and the Tehuantepec genesis area is still high (~80% in 7 days) tracking parallel to southern Mexico — no cyclone near Costa Rica. Gyre/temporales watch stays elevated, not established: ensemble means keep Pacific SW low-level moisture into Nicoya through the weekend into early next week, without a closed land gyre.

IMN Wednesday steps Pacífico Norte up a notch vs Tuesday: morning little–partly cloudy, afternoon scattered showers with storms, and coastal rains tonight (Nicoya ~32°C; Liberia ~36°C). Hurricane Polo and Hurricane Odalys remain well offshore Mexico/west EPAC with no cyclone near Costa Rica; Tehuantepec genesis is now high (~80% in 7 days) but tracks parallel to southern Mexico. Gyre/temporales watch stays elevated, not established — ensemble means keep Pacific SW low-level flow into Nicoya longer than yesterday’s GEFS trade-return signal suggested.

IMN Tuesday keeps Pacífico Norte in a typical ITCZ rainy-season day: isolated morning rains, possible isolated afternoon rain, and possible coastal rains tonight (Nicoya ~33°C). Hurricane Polo and TS Odalys stay well offshore Mexico/west EPAC — no cyclone near Costa Rica. Midweek SW Pacific moisture and flanking EPAC lows still show on ensemble means, but GEFS flips Nicoya back toward trades by ~Sun and NHC marine softens the CR–Guatemala low language, so the gyre/temporales watch stays elevated, not established.

IMN Monday regional keeps a typical rainy-season ITCZ day for Pacífico Norte: isolated afternoon storms and possible coastal rains tonight, with Nicoya heat near 32°C. No tropical cyclone near Costa Rica — TS Polo (ex-EP99) and TS Odalys stay well offshore Mexico/west EPAC. Ensemble means still favor Pacific SW moisture and flanking EPAC lows mid–late week; NHC marine now flags a monsoon low building early Friday between Costa Rica and Guatemala. Gyre watch remains elevated, not established.

IMN Sunday regional keeps an unstable moist ITCZ pattern: Pacífico Norte afternoon isolated storms and possible coastal rains tonight, with Nicoya heat near 32°C (down from yesterday’s ~37°C). OT#45 was Saturday’s story (latest IMN aviso Sat 5:50 p.m.); no tropical cyclone near Costa Rica. Midweek ensemble means still lean Pacific SW moisture / flanking EPAC lows, but the quieter Wed signal pushes the elevated gyre watch later than yesterday’s Tue–Thu window — still a watch, not established.

IMN has tropical wave OT#45 crossing this afternoon–evening with ITCZ interaction and thunderstorms near the Nicoya Peninsula tonight along the Pacific coast, while Nicoya heat climbs near 37°C. No tropical cyclone near Costa Rica; EPAC development stays well offshore southwest of Mexico or farther west. Midweek ensemble means now lean more toward Pacific SW moisture flow and flanking lows than yesterday’s lighter easterlies — still a watch, not a locked temporales.

IMN keeps Pacífico Norte partly cloudy with only a chance of peninsula rain this afternoon, while heat stays near 36°C at Nicoya; tropical waves OT#44 (overnight) and OT#45 (Sunday) plus ITCZ moisture are the weekend–early-week shower drivers. No tropical cyclone near Costa Rica; EPAC development interest remains well offshore southwest of Mexico or farther west, not aimed at Nicoya.

IMN flips today’s Nicoya Peninsula into afternoon/evening showers and thunderstorms as trades ease and Pacific moisture rises, with heat near 36–37°C. No tropical cyclone near Costa Rica; EPAC development interest stays well southwest of Mexico and farther west, not aimed at Nicoya.

IMN has today quieter with only isolated peninsula showers, then a possible humidity/rain bump into Guanacaste this weekend. No tropical cyclone near Costa Rica; EPAC interest stays well offshore southwest of Mexico and trending west.
